title: Airtable personal access token placeholders, references, masks and bare Bearer scheme
summary: A Bearer header with no value, an angle placeholder, an environment reference, a template reference and a masked display, and prose that names the header.
rationale: A bare scheme names no token, and a placeholder, a reference or a masked display stands in for a value kept elsewhere. Airtable documents the Bearer header form (carrier-bearer-header-not-url-parameter) but no placeholder of its own for personal access tokens in the contract, so these forms are the project's controls, not Airtable's. Flagging them would redact documentation and configuration a reader needs.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, redact-secret#1228 Group C). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the values here are a bare scheme, placeholders, references, masks or prose, not credential values; that such forms are not values is a project decision, not an Airtable statement. Airtable documents the Authorization: Bearer header form (carrier existence only).

sources.supports: Personal access tokens should be passed with your API requests as a Authorization: Bearer header.
Passing personal access tokens and OAuth access tokens via the legacy api_key URL parameter is not supported.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
